extracted.intended_audience: community members, civic media producers, partner organizations, and potential Documenters interested in training to attend and report on public meetings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for individuals and partner organizations on training, participating in, and publishing community-powered reporting of local government meetings through the Documenters Network and City Bureau platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend and annotate government meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Public meetings are workshops for democracy, where residents ... can witness, learn about, and act on the systems that impact their lives. Documenters attend and annotate government meetings to create a public record and oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documenters’ presence is described as addressing a systemic failure of the civic information system and creating a powerful new information resource; the work aims to enable residents to witness, learn, and take action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and orientation required
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone can become a Documenter by filling out a Documenters application and attending a Documenters orientation. Network sites bring tried and tested trainings to obtain new skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free, public workshops and orientations are provided so participants can obtain new skills before taking assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paid assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Documenters are paid and their work is used by journalists, organizers, researchers and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants can take on paid assignments after training; payment is an explicit part of the program model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce service-oriented, multi-format reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Documenters produce community-powered reporting — written reports, social media, photos, audio and video — which in many cases is the most complete record of consequential local policy decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All content types are encouraged; outputs are often the primary record of decisions and should be oriented toward public service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff editing and quality control
rubrics_metrics.description: All Documenters Network content is edited by Documenters Network staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff editing is highlighted as part of how community-produced material is shaped and published, implying expectations for review, completeness, and editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish via Documenters.org and the Newswire
rubrics_metrics.description: Results are published via the free, weekly digest the Newswire and the custom web app Documenters.org; the platform enables government accountability reporting and research by creating civic engagement opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the network's platform to publish and preserve records; the platform both distributes work and serves as civic infrastructure for accountability and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate with local journalists and community partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce service-oriented reporting in collaboration with local journalists and partner organizations; Documenters Network sites support partner organizations in communities across the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaboration is core: Documenters’ work is intended to be used by journalists, organizers, and researchers and to strengthen local civic media ecosystems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of community resources and participatory technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Network sites build asset-based and community-focused civic infrastructure by hosting free workshops and social events, online community discussion boards, and participatory technology made by and for people like you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites should provide ongoing community resources (events, discussion boards, tools) to support sustained participation and capacity-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Commons content licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: All Chicago Documenters content is available under Creative Commons, ensuring everyone has access to the information they need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outputs are openly licensed to maximize accessibility and reuse by journalists, researchers, organizers, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on accountability, transparency, and public oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Chicago Documenters is described as a local hub for civic action and public oversight of local government through local media, with a mission to make local government accountable and transparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documenters’ documentation should emphasize accountability and transparency — documenting public governance meetings and civic events with that purpose in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset-based and inclusive community approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Documenters Network sites work to build inclusive and equitable civic ecosystems with local communities; people most harmed by the status quo are most invested in solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should center asset-based approaches and prioritize participation from communities most affected by local policy, reinforcing values of collaboration, openness, responsiveness, and exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network growth and partnership model
rubrics_metrics.description: The Documenters Network launched in Chicago in 2016 and grows with new cities and regions each year; it supports organizations in multiple states and communities to develop their own Documenters sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model includes training partner organizations, developing place-based models, and supporting others to build local hubs — indicating standards for replication, support, and partnership.
